name: Barak
source_summary: Israelite commander summoned by the prophetess Deborah to lead Israel's forces against the Canaanite general Sisera, who agreed only on condition that Deborah accompany him, and later listed among the heroes of faith in Hebrews 11.
family_friendly_summary: Barak was called by the prophetess Deborah to lead Israel's army against a powerful Canaanite general named Sisera, who had 900 iron chariots. Barak agreed to go, but only if Deborah came with him too. Deborah agreed, and told Barak that because of his request, the credit for defeating Sisera would go to a woman instead of to him. God gave Israel the victory just as He had promised, and Barak and Deborah celebrated together afterward with a song of praise. Even though Barak needed some encouragement to step out in faith, the New Testament later remembers him as one of the heroes of faith, showing that God can use even hesitant obedience for great purposes.
adult_story: Barak, from Kedesh in Naphtali, was summoned by the prophetess and judge Deborah with God's specific battle plan: gather ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun at Mount Tabor, and God would draw out Sisera, commander of Canaan's oppressive army with its 900 iron chariots, to be defeated at the Kishon river (Judges 4:6-7). Barak's response reveals a real, if imperfect, faith: 'If you will go with me, then I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go' (4:8) -- he was willing to obey, but only with Deborah's presence assuring him of God's guidance. Deborah agreed to accompany him, though she told him the LORD would deliver Sisera 'into the hands of a woman,' a statement whose fulfillment came not through her but through Jael (4:9, 17-22). Barak did lead the assault that routed Sisera's chariots and army completely, pursuing the survivors himself, even though Sisera fled the scene before Barak could capture him personally (4:14-16, 22). Afterward Barak joined Deborah in the extended victory song of Judges 5, praising God's intervention. Despite his initial hesitation, Hebrews 11:32 lists Barak among the great heroes of faith, alongside Gideon, Samson, and David -- Scripture's own verdict that Barak's obedience, even when it required reassurance, still counted as genuine faith that accomplished God's purposes for Israel.
devotionals: Barak agreed to lead Israel's army against Sisera's iron chariots only on the condition Deborah went with him, an honest, hesitant kind of faith rather than a bold one. Jesus doesn't wait for faith to be fearless before He uses it; Hebrews 11 lists Barak among the heroes anyway.

God had told Deborah that Sisera would fall by a woman's hand, and it happened just as she said, exactly on schedule and exactly as spoken. God's word about Jesus has that same track record of coming true precisely as promised, however the details unfold.
